projects.title: Auth and Billing Migrations
projects.shortDescription: Migration of the login system from AWS Cognito to Keycloak, paired with Stripe billing — giving users single sign-on while their access is automatically tied to their subscription.
projects.longDescription:
This project modernizes how users sign in and pay across the platform. It replaces the previous AWS Cognito login with Keycloak, a more flexible and secure identity system, and connects it to Stripe for billing. The goal is to give users a smoother single sign-on experience while opening the door to paid, subscription-based access.

In practice, users log in once to reach all the connected applications, and what they can access depends directly on their subscription. When someone subscribes, upgrades, or cancels through Stripe, their permissions update automatically — with no manual intervention. The experience stays consistent and always in sync with what each customer is actually paying for.

At the heart of the system is a custom "trust" service, built in Python, that acts as a bridge between the login system (Keycloak) and the payment platform (Stripe), keeping user accounts, roles, and subscriptions in agreement in real time. Running on Kubernetes in the AWS cloud, it is designed to stay reliable and consistent as the number of users grows.

projects.title: High-Performance Routing Orchestrator
projects.shortDescription: A FastAPI REST API that orchestrates intensive maritime routing computations on Amazon EKS — queuing requests through SQS and spinning up compute pods on demand via Argo Events, at scale and reliably.
projects.longDescription:
This service is the **backend engine** that powers **Tactics**, D-ICE's B2B maritime routing software. It acts as the **central entry point** through which the application requests ship route calculations — computing the best possible routes for vessels by accounting for weather, travel time, and fuel — and exposes that capability through a single, consistent **FastAPI** (Python) REST API.

Because these calculations are heavy, incoming requests are queued through **AWS SQS** and picked up by compute pods that are **spun up on demand via Argo Events** inside a Kubernetes cluster on **Amazon EKS**, then scaled back down once the work is done. This lets many routing jobs run in parallel without slowing each other down, and keeps the system **reliable** even during peak demand. Persistent data lives in **AWS RDS (PostgreSQL)**, with **PgBouncer** handling connection pooling so the database stays stable under bursts of parallel workers.

The platform also comes with dedicated observability. A **Grafana** dashboard gives an at-a-glance overview of usage and basic routing visualizations, while a **custom React tool** allows deeper inspection of individual routings — helping to understand why certain calculations failed and to **export results in a decision-support format**, used to guide and support ship captains on the routes they have actually sailed.

Rather than developing the C++ routing engine itself, the project focuses on wrapping it in a **robust, scalable, and highly available** orchestration layer — from the API surface down to the on-demand compute and monitoring — that reliably connects the engine to the applications and clients that depend on it.

projects.title: Weather Data Distribution Platform
projects.shortDescription: A low-latency weather data platform (sub-200ms) that ingests, processes, and distributes multi-source weather data — powering the weather layers and map visualizations of D-ICE's Tactics and SquidX routing software.
projects.longDescription:
This platform ingests, processes, and distributes weather data with very low latency, acting as D-ICE's in-house alternative to services like **Windy**. It feeds the weather layers and **map-based visualizations** of the **Tactics** and **SquidX** maritime routing software, giving navigators a fast, reliable view of current and forecast conditions.

To keep response times **under 200ms**, the platform combines a **distributed cache** (**etcd**) with **in-memory caching** powered by **Dragonfly** (a high-performance, Redis-compatible store) for ultra-fast redistribution. A **predictive preloading** mechanism analyzes usage patterns to load weather data into the cache before it is even requested. It also serves **historical weather data**, produced by a fleet of **workers** running orchestrated batch computations.

The entire platform is built in **Node.js** and runs on **Kubernetes** in the **AWS** cloud. A notable engineering decision shaped the project: C++ optimizations were initially planned but ultimately dropped — the overhead of bridging data between JavaScript and C++ cancelled out the raw compute gains, so a **pure Node.js** implementation proved both faster to build and fast enough in production.

projects.title: Maritime Weather & Routing Desktop App
projects.shortDescription: The desktop and mobile front-end of D-ICE's Tactics and SquidX maritime routing software — letting navigators run and compare route calculations and overlay weather and satellite data on an interactive map.
projects.longDescription:
This is the user-facing application of D-ICE's **Tactics** and **SquidX** maritime routing software — the desktop and mobile front-end that navigators and ship captains rely on at sea. It brings together, in a single interface, the route calculations served by the routing backend and the weather data streamed from the in-house weather platform.

From the app, users can **launch route calculations and compare the proposed trajectories**, **overlay weather and satellite imagery** on an interactive map, and dig into performance through dedicated **statistics panels**.

The desktop application — the core of the project — is built with **React** and **TypeScript** and packaged with **Electron**. A lightweight companion app is built with **React Native**.

projects.title: Information System Mapping & Modernization
projects.shortDescription: Mapping and modernization of a key account's information system: studying the existing setup, designing a microservices architecture to break down legacy monoliths, and implementing a centralized Keycloak authentication service.
projects.longDescription:
As a **software architect** at ASI, I led the mapping and modernization of a key account's information system, with the goal of pooling and streamlining its services. The mission combined analysis, architecture design, and hands-on implementation, together with advisory support to the client throughout.

The work started with a full **study and mapping of the existing IS** to identify what could be shared and consolidated. From there, I designed a target **microservices architecture** to progressively break down legacy **monolithic applications** into smaller, independent services — more scalable and easier to maintain.

A key deliverable was a **centralized authentication service built with Keycloak**, providing unified identity and access management across the system. The stack relied on **Java** for backend services, **React** for the front-end interfaces, and **Microsoft Azure** for hosting — and the role also involved advising the client on modernization and security choices.

projects.title: Software Supervisor

projects.title: HDR vs LDR Visual Attention Comparison
projects.shortDescription: Projet de recherche comparant l'attention visuelle sur des images HDR et LDR à l'aide d'algorithmes d'IA pour déterminer quelle méthode de conversion préserve le mieux les patterns d'attention humaine.
projects.longDescription:
Ce projet de recherche, mené dans le cadre d'études à Polytech, avait pour but de comparer différentes méthodes pour convertir des images très lumineuses (HDR) en images classiques (LDR), tout en conservant la façon dont l'œil humain est attiré par certains éléments de l'image originale.Pour y parvenir, une intelligence artificielle a été entraînée pour apprendre à reconnaître les zones qui attirent le regard sur une image HDR. Cette IA utilisait trois techniques principales :
 - Un système de comparaison (réseau siamois) pour évaluer les différences entre les images.
 - Une méthode d'apprentissage appelée triplet loss, qui permet à l'IA de distinguer plus finement les similitudes et les différences entre trois images à la fois (une image de référence, une image similaire, et une image différente), afin d'affiner ses prédictions.
 - Une mémoire des séquences (couches LSTM) pour analyser comment le regard se déplace dans le temps sur une image.
L'originalité de ce travail réside dans le fait d'avoir combiné ces techniques pour la première fois, en intégrant des données sur le mouvement du regard (données temporelles) dans l'analyse. Grâce à cette méthode, il a été possible de déterminer quels algorithmes de conversion préservent le mieux la perception naturelle de l'image, c'est-à-dire ceux qui gardent une apparence la plus proche de ce que l'œil humain voit et retient.

projects.title: protoruf
projects.shortDescription: A high-performance Python library, written in Rust, for converting data between JSON and Protobuf — faster than Google's standard library and with no tedious setup.
projects.longDescription:
**Protoruf** is a high-performance Python library for two-way conversion between JSON and Protobuf, written in Rust. It removes the tedious, error-prone setup that the usual Protobuf workflow demands: nothing to install or configure by hand, and no generated files to maintain. Developers can change their data structure and keep working instantly, without ever leaving their editor.

Key points:
 - Fast JSON ↔ Protobuf conversion thanks to Rust — up to 10 times faster than Google's standard `google.protobuf` library.
 - Native integration with Pydantic models, for automatic data validation with no extra code.
 - In-memory compilation of .proto files, with no external dependencies (no `protoc` to install).
 - Formatted JSON output and strict typing.

Ideal for projects that need fast, structured and reliable data exchange. Freely available on PyPI with full documentation and a published article explaining the approach.

projects.title: Bot Analyste Quantitatif
projects.shortDescription: Dashboard interactif d'analyse de marché utilisant une convergence de modèles quantitatifs (Machine Learning et statistiques) pour générer des opinions de marché structurées.
projects.longDescription:
Ce projet personnel consiste en un dashboard interactif d'analyse de marché construit avec Streamlit, combinant plusieurs modèles quantitatifs pour générer des signaux de trading structurés. L'application intègre cinq modèles distincts : XGBoost et Random Forest pour la classification directionnelle, ARIMA pour la prévision de prix, GARCH pour l'estimation de la volatilité, et Prophet pour la détection de tendances et de cycles saisonniers.

Le système calcule plus de 100 features techniques incluant les indicateurs de tendance (SMA, EMA), de momentum (RSI, MACD, Stochastic), de volatilité (Bandes de Bollinger, ATR), et de volume (OBV, VWAP, MFI). Il détecte également des patterns de chandeliers japonais et intègre des données fondamentales via Yahoo Finance (ratios de valuation, profitabilité, croissance).

Un système de décision par vote pondéré combine les prédictions des modèles avec des poids optimisés (XGBoost 25%, Random Forest 25%, ARIMA 20%, Prophet 30%), ajustés par la précision de chaque modèle sur le jeu de test. La volatilité GARCH agit comme modificateur de conviction, réduisant la confiance en cas de volatilité élevée.

L'application propose une interface CLI complète pour l'automatisation avec des outils comme n8n ou Zapier, permettant la génération de rapports en JSON, Markdown ou texte. Le projet inclut également une architecture Docker pour le déploiement et des workflows n8n prêts à l'emploi pour l'intégration dans des pipelines d'automatisation.

projects.title: RVaultPass
projects.shortDescription: Un gestionnaire de mots de passe sécurisé, local et zero-knowledge pour desktop, avec chiffrement AES-256 et base de données SQLCipher.
projects.longDescription:
**RVaultPass** est un gestionnaire de mots de passe desktop qui garde l'intégralité de vos données sur votre propre machine — aucun serveur, aucun cloud, aucune donnée transmise sur internet. Tout est stocké dans un seul fichier chiffré.

L'application permet de stocker et organiser tous vos identifiants, notes et codes à usage unique (TOTP) en toute simplicité. Elle propose un générateur de mots de passe fort, des codes TOTP qui se rafraîchissent en temps réel, une recherche instantanée dans tous vos éléments, ainsi qu'une organisation par dossiers et tags. Un système de favoris permet d'accéder rapidement à vos comptes les plus utilisés.

Développé avec **Rust** et **Tauri**, le projet a été conçu avec une approche "zero-knowledge" : l'interface ne voit jamais vos mots de passe en clair, et toutes les opérations sensibles sont traitées directement dans le noyau sécurisé de l'application. Le tout dispose d'une interface bilingue français/anglais avec un thème clair et sombre.

projects.title: Automate Simulator
projects.shortDescription: Logiciel de création, modification et simulation d'automates pour l'IUT de Valence, permettant de concevoir des graphes d'automatisation, les tester, les simplifier, avec un mode examen pour l'évaluation.
projects.longDescription:
L'**Automate Simulator** est un logiciel desktop développé pour l'IUT de Valence, conçu pour faciliter l'apprentissage et la pratique des automates graphiques. Il permet de créer et modifier des graphes d'automatisation, de les simuler pour tester leur bon fonctionnement, et de les simplifier automatiquement grâce à un algorithme dédié.

L'application dispose d'un **mode examen** qui retire la plupart des outils pour ne conserver que les fonctionnalités essentielles : modification du graphe et sauvegarde en PDF. Ce mode permet d'évaluer les étudiants dans des conditions contrôlées, sans accès aux outils d'aide.

Développé en **Java** avec **Swing**, le projet offre une interface graphique complète pour concevoir, tester et exporter des automates, servant d'outil pédagogique pour les étudiants en informatique.

projects.title: Copy Contents
projects.shortDescription: A VS Code extension to copy the entire contents of a folder to your clipboard in one click — ideal for feeding context to LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot).
projects.longDescription:
**Copy Contents** is a Visual Studio Code extension that copies the combined contents of all files within a folder straight to your clipboard in a single click. It is built for developers who want to quickly share code with language models (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot) without opening each file one by one.

Key features:
 - **Copy folder contents**: recursively copy everything in a folder in one click from the context menu.
 - **Selective copy**: a dialog lets you pick exactly which files to include, with a per-folder toggle to check/uncheck all of its files at once.
 - **Multi-selection**: the commands operate on the entire selection (files and/or folders).
 - **Smart filtering**: automatic exclusion of common folders (`.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, etc.), configurable extensions, and file size / count limits.
 - **Structured output**: each file is prefixed with a header showing its path (optional) to help the LLM understand the project layout.

Built with TypeScript, the extension is published on the Visual Studio Marketplace.

projects.title: Best Start
projects.shortDescription: A "best start" optimization service that runs thousands of routing simulations per day to predict travel time on the first leg of a voyage and recommend the optimal departure — consistently beating the previously planned start.
projects.longDescription:
**Best Start** helps ship operators leave at the right moment. It runs **thousands of routing simulations every day** to predict how long the first leg of a voyage will take under different departure conditions, then recommends the **optimal start** — one that improves on the previously planned departure and shortens the overall trip.

Each request fans out into many parallel routing computations. Incoming jobs are queued through **AWS SQS** and picked up by compute pods **spun up on demand via Argo Events** on **Amazon EKS**, so the platform absorbs large daily volumes and scales up or down automatically. Results are stored in **PostgreSQL**, with **PgBouncer** managing connection pooling to keep the database stable under heavy parallel load.

The service is built as a **FastAPI** (Python) backend paired with a **Vue.js** front-end for configuring runs and visualizing the recommended departures. Containerized with **Docker** and running on **Kubernetes** in the **AWS** cloud, it is designed to handle its high daily throughput reliably.

In practice, Best Start contributed to a landmark achievement: it helped optimize the opening leg of **Sodebo Ultim 3**'s campaign, which set a new **Jules Verne Trophy** world record on **January 25, 2026** (round-the-world in 40d 10h) — including a record-breaking **North Atlantic descent** (Ushant to the equator) on the very first part of the course.
